problem_statement: An open-top box is to be made by cutting congruent squares of side length $x$ from the corners of a square piece of cardboard with side length 18 cm and folding up the sides. The side length of the cut-out square that maximizes the volume of the box is [BLANK_1] cm, and the corresponding maximum volume is [BLANK_2] cm$^3$.
solution:
$$ 
\begin{aligned}
& \text{1. Define the volume function.} \\
& \text{Let } x \text{ be the side length of the square cut from each corner.} \\
& \text{The dimensions of the resulting box will be:} \\
& \text{Height: } H = x \\
& \text{Length: } L = 18 - 2x \\
& \text{Width: } W = 18 - 2x \\
& \text{The volume } V(x) \text{ is given by } V(x) = L \cdot W \cdot H = (18 - 2x)(18 - 2x)x = (18 - 2x)^2 x. \\

& \text{2. Determine the feasible domain.} \\
& \text{The side length } x \text{ must be positive, so } x > 0. \\
& \text{The length of the box side must also be positive: } 18 - 2x > 0 \implies 2x < 18 \implies x < 9. \\
& \text{So, the domain for } x \text{ is } (0, 9). \\

& \text{3. Find the derivative of the volume function.} \\
& V(x) = (324 - 72x + 4x^2)x = 4x^3 - 72x^2 + 324x. \\
& V'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}(4x^3 - 72x^2 + 324x) = 12x^2 - 144x + 324. \\

& \text{4. Find the critical points.} \\
& \text{Set } V'(x) = 0 \text{ and solve for } x: \\
& 12x^2 - 144x + 324 = 0 \\
& \text{Divide by 12: } x^2 - 12x + 27 = 0 \\
& \text{Factor the quadratic: } (x-3)(x-9) = 0. \\
& \text{The critical points are } x = 3 \text{ and } x = 9. \\

& \text{5. Select the valid critical point and verify it is a maximum.} \\
& \text{The critical point } x=9 \text{ is not in the domain } (0, 9). \\
& \text{The only critical point in the domain is } x = 3. \\
& \text{We use the Second Derivative Test to confirm this is a maximum.} \\
& V''(x) = \frac{d}{dx}(12x^2 - 144x + 324) = 24x - 144. \\
& V''(3) = 24(3) - 144 = 72 - 144 = -72. \\
& \text{Since } V''(3) < 0, \text{ the volume is maximized at } x = 3. \\

& \text{6. Calculate the maximum volume.} \\
& \text{Substitute } x=3 \text{ into the volume function } V(x). \\
& V(3) = (18 - 2(3))^2 (3) = (18 - 6)^2 (3) = (12)^2 (3) = 144 \times 3 = 432. \\

& \text{The side length of the cut is 3 cm, and the maximum volume is 432 cm}^3.
\end{aligned}
$$

scaffolding.hint: First, express the volume of the box as a function of a single variable, $x$. To do this, determine the length, width, and height of the box after the squares are cut and the sides are folded up.

To find the value of $x$ that maximizes the volume, find the critical points of the volume function $V(x)$. Calculate the derivative $V'(x)$, set it to zero, and solve for $x$. Remember to check which of these values lies in the feasible domain of the problem.
After finding the optimal value for $x$, substitute it back into your original volume function $V(x)$ to find the maximum possible volume.
